headline: Deep-sea canyon yields 57 new species in two weeks
meta_description: Scientists discovered 57 new marine species in Argentina's Mar del Plata Canyon during a livestreamed expedition that captivated 4 million viewers.
summary_short: A viral sea star may have stolen the spotlight, but Argentina's deep-sea canyon revealed far greater treasures: 57 newly identified species in just 14 days.
body:
A two-week expedition into Argentina's Mar del Plata Canyon has unveiled 57 species previously unknown to science, along with five entirely new genera. The discovery came from a 2025 research expedition that livestreamed deep-sea exploration to more than 4 million viewers worldwide—many tuning in specifically for an orange sea star bearing an uncanny resemblance to the cartoon character Patrick Star. While the famous starfish turned out to be a known species and was left undisturbed on the seafloor, the real treasure trove proved far larger: 22 new echinoderms including sea cucumbers nicknamed Loki, 20 copepods, 14 corals and sea pens, and one tusk-shaped mollusk. Scientists examined only 10 percent of the copepod samples collected, yet every single specimen they studied was new to science—suggesting the canyon harbors vastly more undiscovered life waiting in the remaining 90 percent of samples.

The canyon's extraordinary biodiversity stems from its geographic position as a crossroads where two currents collide. The warm Brazil current flows south while the cold, nutrient-rich Malvinas current sweeps north from sub-Antarctic waters. Where they meet, nutrients fuel explosive biological diversity in a canyon plunging over 3,500 meters deep—nearly twice the Grand Canyon's depth.

Yet even this remote habitat shows the fingerprints of human impact. During just 10 dives, researchers documented 29 pieces of litter scattered across the seafloor, from plastic bags to fishing gear, with one piece of plastic packaging found at nearly 3,814 meters below the surface. The discovery adds urgency to ongoing conservation efforts along Argentina's coast, where researchers have also identified what may be one of the world's largest cold-water coral reefs—itself threatened by potential oil and gas exploration.
quick_facts: 57 new species discovered in Mar del Plata Canyon, Argentina
2025 expedition livestreamed to 4 million global viewers
20 copepods found, 90% of samples still unexamined
Canyon plunges 3,500+ meters deep, nearly twice Grand Canyon depth
29 pieces of litter found during 10 deep-sea dives
